To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neurotoxin BOAA induced a highly selective hippocampal damage pattern identical to that seen with AMPAA and this damage was prevented in a concentration-dependent manner by focal injection of four potential free-radical scavengers.

BOAA-induced neurodegeneration is prevented by the free radical scavengers dimethyl sulphoxide, dimethylthioureas, dimethylformamide and mannitol, suggesting a possible role for free radical formation in the mechanism of neurodegeneration induced by BOAA.
